title: Trump Promises $5,000 'Dividend' Checks to Every American Adult if Republicans Keep Congress
detail: Closing out the RNC's first-ever midterm convention at Dallas's American Airlines Center on Thursday, September 10, 2026, President Trump pledged that every American adult citizen would receive a $5,000 check — which he dubbed the 'Trump dividend' — if Republicans retain control of the House and Senate in November. 'If the Republicans win, you win with us and you get $5,000,' Trump told the crowd, offering no detail on funding mechanics, though Vice President Vance had indicated tariff revenue would partly cover the cost. With roughly 245 million US adult citizens, the payout would total an estimated $1.2 trillion. Tax Foundation economist Erica York said the checks would 'spend almost all the revenue that the new tariffs are projected to bring in over a decade,' and former IMF chief economist Kenneth Rogoff warned it would 'blow up' an already unsustainable deficit; election-law scholar Rick Hasen said Trump likely has First Amendment latitude to make the campaign promise (citing Brown v. Hartlage) but actual payments would require congressional approval. Similar Trump pledges in 2025 — a tariff dividend and a DOGE dividend — never materialized. In the same speech Trump also vowed to make his tax cuts permanent, pursue 'most-favored-nation' prescription drug pricing, redirect health-insurer payments directly to citizens, and told the crowd 'you go to hell' if they don't vote in November.

media.caption: Trump pledged $5,000 'Trump dividend' checks to Americans if Republicans keep Congress in the midterms

title: Denver, LULAC Sue Trump Administration to Keep Armed ICE Agents Away From Polling Places
detail: The City and County of Denver, joined by LULAC, Common Cause, UnidosUS and other voting-rights groups, filed suit Thursday, September 10, 2026, in federal court in Washington, D.C. against Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, challenging the Trump-Vance administration's September 1 policy authorizing armed ICE officers to enter polling places to serve warrants or conduct immigration-enforcement activity during the November 2026 midterms. The suit invokes 18 U.S.C. § 592, a Civil War-era law barring armed federal forces from polling places, arguing the policy amounts to voter intimidation aimed at Latino communities. Denver Mayor Mike Johnston said 'the right to vote without fear of intimidation is fundamental to democracy. Stationing ICE agents near polling places is only meant to scare people and suppress votes.' A DHS spokesperson countered that ICE has no operation specifically targeting polling locations planned but could make arrests at a site it deems an 'active public safety threat.' The complaint cites ICE activity near polling places in San Antonio, Ventura County, and Syracuse during May-June 2026 primaries, though none occurred in Colorado.

media.caption: Denver and Latino civil-rights groups sued to block armed ICE agents from polling places ahead of the midterms
